requirement: Create a test account at pgai.us/athena to understand the patient experience.
Do not call the number on the account confirmation screen.
All assessment calls go only to +18054398008.
Simulate realistic patient scenarios and identify target bugs or quality issues.
Record and transcribe conversations.

Use Python and LiveKit Agents in pipeline mode with separate STT, text LLM and TTS; provider choice is open.

Include working Python code in the private GitHub repository.

Submit at least ten complete conversations, both sides recorded and transcribed; typically one to three minutes, not question-and-hang-up.
Submit actual audio recordings in OGG or MP3 as well as transcripts.
Bug report makes clear what happened, why it is a problem and where evidence can be found; example format is optional.
Project walkthrough video is at most three minutes and communicates approach and reasoning.
Do not use Pretty Good AI or PGAI in Loom presentation language.
Use webcam/video and your own voice in the required videos.
Provide a second screen recording showing genuine iterative AI prompting to debug/fix code and prompts used at each step.
Keep code clean, readable and reasonably structured.
Document needed API keys and environment variables; do not commit secrets.
Include .env.example showing needed variables.
Do not use Pretty Good AI or PGAI in repository name, description or README title.
Keep the repository private after submission.
Cover appointment scheduling, reschedule/cancel, refills, office hours/location/insurance and interruption/unclear/unusual cases.
Expected project time is up to six hours; deeper useful analysis and creative edge cases can distinguish the submission.
First review is call audio: coherent conversation is the highest priority and a rejection gate.
Useful well-described bugs beat a long list of nitpicks.
Code must actually make real telephone calls.
Explain STT, LLM, TTS, turn detection, interruptions, phone connectivity, latency, alternatives and tradeoffs in architecture/Loom.
Show improvements based on early call results.
Follow all instructions rigorously and provide understandable code.
Perfect code, overengineering, fancy diagrams, punctuation nitpicks, one-shot copy-paste and production infrastructure are not the goal.
Calls have natural conversational interaction and sensible turn taking except intentional barge-in tests.
Actively steer toward the scenario outcome while preserving realistic pacing and flow.
Audio is clear with minimal glitches, latency, unintended interruptions or awkward pauses; caller behaves like a real user.

Complete the assessment submission form with private repository URL and reviewer access.
Include both videos; debugging video is viewable by anyone with the link.
Use one originating number for all calls and submit that exact number in E.164 format.
